clue.text: Gutted lad left, after game, for a drink

indicators.note: the boy-and-left pieces come after the game in the answer

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: a gutted thing has had its insides removed, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: a lad is a boy
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A drinker orders something after the match while a skinny youth departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' takes the middle O out of BOY, leaving BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby port is a red fortified wine, served as a drink.

clue.text: Travel free, heading for Egypt

parts.note: to rid is to free

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone travels at no cost on their way to Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle, a synonym.

clue.text: Having completed a circuit, but no further forward?

definitions.text: Having completed a circuit, but no further forward?

parts.words: Having completed a circuit, but no further forward?
parts.note: going all the way round a board game route leaves you where you began, an idiom for making no progress

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means returning to the starting point after effort, with no progress made.

clue.text: Base of statue may be newly plastered right away

indicators.note: newly means the letters are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: The base of a statue may be freshly plastered at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' takes R from PLASTERED, and 'newly' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base on which a statue stands.

clue.text: Hoist ladder at university

parts.note: a ladder in tights is a run
up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a ladder up at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladder' looks like the climbing tool but is a stocking run; 'up' for being at university is British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up a flag is to hoist it, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Eccentric American, writer on cricket

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: An odd American turns out to be a cricket writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Neville Cardus was a famous English cricket writer for the Manchester Guardian; cricket is a bat-and-ball game hugely popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Neville Cardus is the best-known cricket journalist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Bent of chief journalist

parts.note: arch means chief, as in archenemy
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Something about the inclination of a senior journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as a noun (inclination) but is the adjective curved.
explanation.definitionFit: Arched means curved, which bent can mean.

clue.text: Forced into an awkward situation, as coach party may be visiting China?

definitions.text: as coach party may be visiting China?
definitions.meaning: tourists on a coach would be taken by road to the Great Wall

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pushed to ruin; read literally it describes a bus trip to the Great Wall.

clue.text: "Wells Fargo" and "Deadwood," say —- travelling players used them

definitions.meaning: names of stagecoaches or lines in the Wild West

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers coach-line names in Western lore and the professional names performers adopt.

clue.text: Rebuke agent and film producer

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
Hal Roach produced Laurel and Hardy films

explanation.surface: A sales agent and a movie producer get a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Hal Roach was the Hollywood producer behind Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach is to rebuke, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Northern church after a number of years in decline

indicators.note: after sends the northern church pieces behind the years in the answer

parts.note: a decade is ten years
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A northern church has been falling into decline for years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' could be a verb, but it is the noun the answer defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is moral or cultural decline, a near-synonym.

clue.text: What's tea passed round in?

indicators.note: the tea is put around the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: cha (char) is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A question about the crockery from which tea is served.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is old British slang for tea, and the clue's picture is true too: tea is handed round in porcelain cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain crockery, the cups in which tea is handed round, is called after the country.

clue.text: Ring rest back to expose a US inventor

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: back says the word for rest is read from right to left

parts.note: to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: Someone resting reveals an American inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Elisha Otis invented the safety elevator; 'Ring' as O is a standard crossword shape convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisha Otis was the American who invented the safety lift brake.

clue.text: Soldier on exercises runs hard

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
severe means hard or harsh

explanation.surface: A soldier is drilled with exercises and hard running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks like a noun but is the verb in 'soldier on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to keep going despite difficulty, an idiom for persisting.

clue.text: Wayward type beginning to seduce head girl

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a cape is a headland
Grace is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A rogue starts to seduce the head girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head girl' looks like the school prefect but splits into headland and a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegrace is a mischievous rascal, a wayward person.

clue.text: Narcotics bust involving a person from San Jos, perhaps

indicators.note: involving means taking in the next piece
a bust is a police raid, but here the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Police raid a drug haul, catching someone from Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' rearranges NARCOTICS and 'involving' takes in A. San José (printed here without its accent) is the capital of Costa Rica.
explanation.definitionFit: San José is the Costa Rican capital, so a resident there is an example of the nationality.

clue.text: TV showing fool fight

parts.note: an idiot is a fool
to box is to fight

explanation.surface: Television shows a fool in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for television, mocking it as mindless.

clue.text: Greek leaving Scottish village for high peak

indicators.note: leaving means the Greek abbreviation departs from the village name

parts.note: Gretna (Green) is a Scottish border village famous for runaway weddings

explanation.surface: A Greek quits a Scottish village for the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green is the village just over the Scottish border where eloping English couples married.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the tall volcano on Sicily, so a high peak.

clue.text: Sweet shot may hit this window

definitions.meaning: a thick glass pane with a central boss

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a mint sweet, the centre of a target and a disc of bottle glass in a window.

clue.text: Choice fruit

definitions.meaning: a ... job or role is a choice, desirable one
the stone fruit of the genus Prunus

explanation.definitionFit: Plum is both an adjective for a prize position and the name of a common stone fruit.

clue.text: Outline alterations to be made to hotel suite

indicators.note: alterations means the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A designer sketches the outline of planned changes to a hotel suite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alterations to be made to' rearranges HOTEL SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is a dark outline shape seen against light.

clue.text: Composer averse to change

indicators.note: to change means the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer is reluctant to alter anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges AVERSE. Edgard Varèse was a French-American modernist composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgard Varese was a pioneering twentieth-century composer of electronic music.

clue.text: Giant fish a month back swallowing worker

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: swallowing means the month takes in the worker
back means the month abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Aug is short for August
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A huge fish, a month later, gulps down an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: GUA (the month read backwards) is split open by the worker. Gargantua is the giant of Rabelais's sixteenth-century satire.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantua is the enormous giant of Rabelais's satire, so the name of a giant.

clue.text: Change flag when heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to flag is to falter or tire

explanation.surface: A flag is changed when its top part comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning to tire.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter is to change, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Romantic song told a story

definitions.meaning: a German art song of the Romantic era, as by Schubert
told a fib, said something untrue

explanation.definitionFit: Lied is a German Romantic song, and also the past tense of the verb meaning fibbed.

clue.text: Joy requires shelter after onset of gale

indicators.note: after puts the shelter piece behind the gale letter
the onset of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side

explanation.surface: Joy needs some cover once the storm begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great delight, a synonym for joy.

clue.text: On one's own in plant around noon

indicators.note: around means the plant goes about the noon letter

parts.note: aloe is a succulent plant

explanation.surface: Someone sits by themselves among the plants at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts ALOE around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Being by oneself, without company, is a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Alert, having just received a pass?

definitions.meaning: a footballer who has just been passed to has possession at their feet

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being sharp and attentive literally describes a player in possession after a pass.

clue.text: Level, holding the Parisian football team

indicators.note: holding means the word for level contains the French article

parts.note: even means level
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A Paris football side holds level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'football team' is the side's size: an association football team fields this many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side has eleven players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Right-winger, actual Oxford team member

parts.note: true means actual, real
a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge university at sport

explanation.surface: A conservative is actually a member of an Oxford team.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is a sportsperson who played for Oxford or Cambridge against the other; true blue means staunchly Conservative in Britain, whose party colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: True blue describes a loyal Tory, a staunch right-wing conservative in British usage.
